desc:
Weekly and monthly ecommerce sales reports turn raw store numbers into a short story about what happened and what to do next. Ecom Swift LLC pulls your sales data, checks it for gaps and writes a plain-language report with clear actions.

## What is a plain-language sales report?

A plain-language sales report explains your numbers in sentences instead of leaving you with a table to decode. It states what happened to revenue, orders and average order value, which products moved, and what likely caused the change. It ends with a few actions you can take.

Store admin screens show data, but they rarely tell you what matters this week. Most owners look at the totals, feel unsure what to make of them and move on. A written report closes that gap.

## Why regular reporting improves decisions

Sales rarely move without a reason. A promotion, a new ad, a stock shortage, a price change or a slow shipping week can each shift results. When you review your numbers on a steady rhythm, you connect those causes to effects while you still remember them. At month end, nobody remembers why the second week was strong.

Reports also protect you from small, slow problems. A product whose sales fade a little each month, a discount that cuts margin more than it adds orders, or a traffic source that stops converting can all hide in daily noise. A weekly or monthly view reveals them.

Lastly, a report helps other people. An accountant, partner or investor can read it without learning your store, and a team can agree on priorities from the same page.

## What a useful sales report includes

- Revenue, order count and average order value for the period.
- A comparison with the previous period and the same period earlier.
- A best sellers list and a bottom sellers list, with a note on each.
- Traffic sources and conversion rate, so sales link to marketing.
- A discount summary showing how much of your revenue used codes.
- Returns and refunds, so net sales are not overstated.
- Repeat customers against first-time buyers, where data allows.
- Ad spend set beside the sales it relates to.
- Two or three charts that show the trend at a glance.
- Three suggested actions, written as specific steps.

## How we produce your report

We begin by agreeing which period and which sources to cover. Then we pull orders and product data from your store and traffic and campaign data from analytics and ad accounts. Before writing anything, we check the data: do totals match the store, are refunds counted, did tracking break on any day? If something looks wrong, we note it instead of building a story on weak ground.

Next we write. We explain the headline numbers, point out what changed and give our best reading of why, labeled honestly as a likely cause rather than a proven one. We choose charts that show the point and leave out the rest.

The starter sprint comes in three levels. Basic delivers one written report on a single month. Standard delivers three weekly reports with traffic, discounts and returns. Premium delivers a monthly report with customer views, ad spend against sales, a product group view, a reusable sheet template and a review call. Ongoing monthly reporting is quoted separately, so you know exactly what the sprint covers.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Read the report with last month's open, so changes are easy to spot.
- Act on one or two suggestions at a time.
- Tell us about promotions and stock issues in the period.
- Keep your product names and categories tidy.
- Share the report with the people who make spending decisions.

**Avoid:**
- Judging a week by a single day of results.
- Chasing every dip without checking returns and stock.
- Comparing months that include different promotions as if they were equal.
- Ignoring cost data when you look at sales alone.
- Treating a likely cause as a certainty.

## Who sales reports are for

They suit owners who are good at the product and less comfortable with spreadsheets. They help busy founders who want a monthly view without building it themselves, and stores that need something to share with an accountant, a partner or a lender. A store with a recent launch can use a first report as a baseline for later comparisons.

## What we need from you

We need viewer or staff access to your store, and viewer access to your analytics and ad accounts if you want traffic and spend included. Tell us the period, your goals and any events that affected sales, such as a sale or stock shortage. If you track costs, share product costs so we can discuss profit. We never ask for passwords, and the report is yours to share.
